title: fix(console): the sign-in page finishes the mobile sign-in hand-off instead of landing on a missing Console page
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB9ZFKq8kvUEM1zfaJkpDrs7)_

Fixes #29971

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：Console 的登录页（和注册页）在 `?redirect=` 恰好指向移动端 hand-off 路由时，登录后直接用脚本跳过去（不再拼进 `/_console`），并且排在选组织之前；浏览器里已有的会话若超过 5 分钟，先显示登录表单，重新登录后再跳。
- **为什么改**：移动端在系统浏览器里打开登录页完成 Google 等登录后，本该跳到 hand-off 拿 302 回 App，现在却落在「页面不存在」，服务端在 18.3.0 已上线的那一半没人能用到。
- **风险与回滚**：只认 hand-off 这一条路径（同源、同 auth base、路径完全相等），其他所有 redirect 行为不变；回滚即 revert 本 PR，登录页回到旧行为。
- **先看**：`ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts`（`handoffNavigationTarget` 的匹配条件、`useHandoffRedirect` 的五分钟判定），`LoginPage.tsx` 登录后编排里新增的第 2 步。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/signInHandoff-29971.test.tsx apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/handoffRedirect-29971.test.ts`，预期 2 个文件、29 条全部通过。
- **需要你做的**：这是会话转移（auth）流程，请维护者审阅并合并本 PR。

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## Design: the five-minute session

**What the auth client exposes (measured).** `createAuthClient().getSession()` hands back the `session` object of better-auth's `get-session` answer as received, so the server's `createdAt` is there at runtime even though `AuthClientSession` does not declare it: a `Date` through better-auth's client JSON parser (it revives ISO dates), an ISO string through the raw-`fetch` stale-bearer retry. A sign-in answer is different: `/sign-in/email` answers `{ redirect, token, url, user }`, so after a password sign-in the provider holds `session: undefined` (two-factor and phone sign-ins hold `{ token }`). No new endpoint and no change to `@object-ui/auth` was needed.

**The choice: re-authenticate on top of the old session, not sign it out first.** On a hand-off redirect, a session older than five minutes keeps the ordinary sign-in form on screen; signing in on it creates a new session, the sign-in answer sets this browser's session cookie to it, and the page forwards. Why not sign the old session out first:

1. `signOut()` in the auth client navigates to the provider's end-session URL whenever the server answers one (RP-initiated logout for a federated session). For a visitor whose stale session came from SSO, that takes the browser off the sign-in page and ends the hand-off attempt.
2. On Android, Custom Tabs share Chrome's cookies, which is exactly how a stale session arrives. Signing it out also signs the user out of the web Console in Chrome; signing in on top only replaces this browser's cookie.
3. It adds a request with its own failure leg (a sign-out that fails leaves the state unknown) and buys nothing: the hand-off route is the authority on freshness and refuses an old session itself.

The cost, stated: the old session row is not revoked; it stays valid until it expires, with no cookie in this browser pointing at it. A visitor may sign in as a different account on that form; the hand-off then carries the account they signed in as.

**How "older than five minutes" is decided.** Each session the page holds is judged once, when it arrives, in a layout effect (the clock is never read during render): with a `createdAt`, its age decides (`HANDOFF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS`, restating the route's `ONE_TIME_TOKEN_HANDOFF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`); without one, the session is fresh only if it is not the one the first session check answered, which means a sign-in on this page made it. A session found on arrival with no `createdAt`, or one not judged yet, holds the form. A wrong verdict on the page is never a security question (the route refuses on its own clock); it only decides between showing the form and forwarding to the route's own `401`.

## What changes

- `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts` (new): `handoffNavigationTarget` answers the navigation target for a redirect that names the hand-off, or `null`. The route is built with the spec's `getAuthEndpointUrl(base, 'oneTimeTokenHandoff')` over the auth base every Console auth page uses (`VITE_SERVER_URL` + `/api/v1/auth`, the URL `App.tsx` hands `AuthProvider`). A match needs a root-relative redirect on this page's origin whose parsed path equals the route's path exactly; the answer is re-serialized from the parsed URL. `useHandoffRedirect` adds the five-minute verdict above.
- `LoginPage.tsx`: the post-sign-in orchestration gains a step 2, after the OAuth `/oauth2/authorize` replay and before the organization steps: a hand-off target is navigated to once with `window.location.assign`, unprefixed; a session the route would refuse returns without navigating, and the page renders its form for it (the bootstrap probe for the sign-up offer runs for that visitor as for a signed-out one). Every other redirect keeps `withConsoleBase`.
- `RegisterPage.tsx`: the same step in its post-sign-up orchestration (rules 1 to 4), so a user who follows "Sign up" from the system auth session ends on the hand-off too.
- One `@object-ui/console` patch changeset.

Rule 2 needs no code: the social buttons' default `callbackURL` is the current page, and neither page passes the hand-off as one; a pin holds that.

## Why

The mobile shell (objectstack-ai/mobile#148) opens the Console's sign-in page in the system auth session because some providers refuse embedded WebViews. The server half (#29766) answers the hand-off with `302 SCHEME://…?token=T`, but the sign-in page treated the redirect as a Console route and the browser landed on a Console page that does not exist.

## Tests

<details><summary>New pins (2 files, 29 tests)</summary>

`pages/auth/__tests__/handoffRedirect-29971.test.ts` (the matcher and the verdict):
- the route the spec names under the auth base; the hand-off path with its query answers itself, unprefixed;
- CONTROL `/api/v1/data/x`, `/settings`, `/` answer `null`;
- lookalikes answer `null`: `…/handoffX`, a trailing slash, an extra segment, `…/verify`, upper case, an encoded slash, the path under `/_console`;
- a different base path (`/tenant-a/api/v1/auth`) both ways;
- absolute, protocol-relative, backslash-smuggled and tab-smuggled URLs, and `javascript:`;
- an auth base on another origin;
- the five-minute window (4 min, exactly 5, 6 min, a week), a `Date` or an ISO string, a session without `createdAt` found on arrival vs made by a sign-in, an unreadable `createdAt`.

`pages/auth/__tests__/signInHandoff-29971.test.tsx` (the real `AuthProvider` over a mock client, the Console mounted as the shipped embeddable build, `base href /_console/`):
- rule 1: the hand-off is assigned unprefixed and lands on the route's path; CONTROL `/api/v1/data/x` lands on `/_console/api/v1/data/x`; a lookalike lands under `/_console`; an absolute `https://evil.example…` lands on `/_console/`;
- rule 2: a provider sign-in's `callbackURL` and `errorCallbackURL` are this sign-in page, carrying the hand-off in `?redirect=`, and nothing navigates;
- rule 3: several organizations with none active go to the hand-off, not `/organizations`; a single organization whose activation never answers still goes to the hand-off;
- rule 4: a 6-minute-old session shows the form and does not navigate; a sign-in on that form forwards; a session found without `createdAt` is held; a visitor who arrives signed out is forwarded once signed in; CONTROL: an hour-old session on `?redirect=/settings` still forwards as today;
- RegisterPage: a fresh session goes to the hand-off; CONTROL `/api/v1/data/x`; a 6-minute-old session shows the sign-up form and a sign-up on it forwards.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (the hand-off branch dropped)</summary>

Run under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `LoginPage.tsx`: the anchor `    if (handoff.target) {` replaced by `    if (false && handoff.target) {` (anchor hits 1 → 0, blob `5339378f1236` → `98b3e8304e15`), then `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/signInHandoff-29971.test.tsx -t LoginPage`:

- `Tests  7 failed | 5 passed | 3 skipped (15)` (the 3 skipped are the RegisterPage pins, outside `-t LoginPage`).
- Red: rule 1 "navigates to the hand-off unprefixed, outside the Console mount" (`assign` called twice, not once), both rule-3 pins (`expected './api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff?…' to be '/api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff?r…'`: the old `withConsoleBase` target, which lands under `/_console/`), and four rule-4 pins.
- Green under the ablation, as they should be: the three rule-1 CONTROL/lookalike/absolute pins, rule 2, and the rule-4 CONTROL on `?redirect=/settings`.
- Restored: blob back to `5339378f1236` (= HEAD), `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **RegisterPage: handled.** The same step, rules 1 to 4, in its post-sign-up orchestration. Not changed: its `verificationCallbackURL`. When a deployment requires email verification, the verification mail's link still resolves `?redirect=` as a Console route. That link opens from the mail app, outside the system auth session the mobile shell is waiting on, so a hand-off from there could not return to the app anyway. Whether the shell wants a sign-up that needs verification to come back some other way is the mobile card's call, not this page's.
- **`os serve` cannot register an app scheme (out of scope, server/cli lane).** `packages/cli` composes `AuthPlugin` without `trustedAppSchemes`, and neither a stack's config nor a settings key or env var reaches it (0 hits for `trustedAppSchemes` under `packages/cli` and `packages/runtime`). Measured on a stock `pnpm dev:crm` boot: a signed-in, same-origin `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff?redirect_uri=ai.objectos.mobile://auth/callback…` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, with the message: The "redirect_uri" scheme "ai.objectos.mobile" is not a registered app scheme, so no token is handed to it. A deployment registers the app schemes it hands sign-ins to in its auth configuration. That boot has no auth configuration that could register one. The live check below therefore used a local, measurement-only one-line patch to `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`; it was never committed, and the source and the cli dist were restored afterwards.
- **Drift risk.** `HANDOFF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS` restates plugin-auth's `ONE_TIME_TOKEN_HANDOFF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`, because that module is server-only and this card does not touch `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/**` or `packages/spec/**`. If the server window changes, the page's copy decides only whether a visitor sees the form or the route's own `401`; the route stays the authority.
- **Fails closed.** With a `VITE_SERVER_URL` on another origin, the matcher answers `null` and the redirect keeps today's Console-route behaviour. A skewed client clock moves only the verdict on a session found on arrival (form vs the route's `401`); a session made by a sign-in on the page carries no `createdAt` and is judged as made here.
- **Lint.** eslint on the touched files: 0 errors, 5 warnings. Four are the existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` warnings in the two pages; one is new, the same rule (warn level), on the layout effect that records the verdict in `handoffRedirect.ts`.
- **Type-check coverage of the new test files: not shown.** The Console `type-check` exited 0 and its tsconfig includes `src`, but a `--listFiles` count for the two new test files read 0, so I do not claim they are type-checked by that lane (vitest compiles them without type-checking).

## Verification

All on head `c6ac92e1`; the builds and test runs under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, their exit codes read from its `VERDICT command-exit` line:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` (the closure) | exit 0 (9m32s) |
| `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run` on the two new files | 2 files, 29 / 29 passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console run build` then `run type-check` | exit 0 (2m55s) |
| `node ui/scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` on that build | 2109.4 KB gzipped over 104 of 2401 chunks, budget 2431.6 KB (headroom 322.2 KB); `vendor-objectstack`, where the new module lands, 577.4 / 823.0 KB. No `main` baseline measured. |
| `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --project @object-ui/console` | 295 / 295 files, 2870 / 2870 tests, exit 0 (20m43s) |
| eslint on the touched files | 0 errors, 5 warnings (see Acceptance notes) |
| `node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` (+ `--self-test`) | exit 0, exit 0 |
| `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` | 34 commands, every one exit 0 |
| `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` | `34 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 34 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED` |

**Live, in a browser** (Playwright Chromium against `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh`, the Console built from this head and served at `/_console/`, the dev-seeded admin; the CLI carried the measurement-only `trustedAppSchemes: ['ai.objectos.mobile']` noted above):

- **Fresh sign-in.** `/_console/login?redirect=` naming the hand-off, then a password sign-in on the form: the browser's next navigation is `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff?redirect_uri=ai.objectos.mobile%3A%2F%2Fauth%2Fcallback&code_challenge=…&code_challenge_method=S256` with `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, answered `302` with `Location: ai.objectos.mobile://auth/callback?token=` and a token (redacted in the log). No "page not found". Headless Chromium has no handler for the app scheme, so the tab stays put after the `302`; on a device the system auth session hands that URL to the app.
- **CONTROL.** The same sign-in on `?redirect=/api/v1/data/x` navigates to `/_console/api/v1/data/x`, a Console route, as before.
- **A session older than five minutes.** A browser signed in at 21:39:21Z (`get-session` `createdAt` read back), opened on the hand-off redirect at 21:45:00Z: the sign-in form is shown and no hand-off request is made. The route itself answers that session's cookie with `401`. Signing in on the form then ends in the same `302` with a token, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. The old session still answers `get-session` afterwards, as the design above says (not revoked).
- **Provider sign-in: NOT MEASURED live.** The container has no identity provider (`/api/v1/auth/config` lists no social providers). Rule 2 is held by the unit pin above.
